handfixes.summary: doctor, the CLI error path and the MCP error path all point at `crowdstrike-cli auth login` instead of a nonexistent `auth setup` subcommand (issue #277, #278)
handfixes.why: This CLI's `auth` parent defines login, status, set-token and logout. It has never defined `setup`, yet three generated surfaces told operators to run it: doctor.go's auth_hint (fires when cfg.AuthHeader() is empty), helpers.go's HTTP 400/401/403 remediation, and internal/mcp/tools.go's tool-error text -- 7 occurrences in all. Cobra does not error on an unknown subcommand of a NON-root parent (legacyArgs only rejects unknown args for the root), and the generated parent runs parentNoSubcommandRunE, which returns cmd.Help() -- a nil error. So `crowdstrike-cli auth setup` printed help and exited 0. There was no 'unknown command' error and no non-zero exit anywhere in the journey: an operator saw a success code and was no closer to credentials, and because these are agent-first CLIs with typed exit codes, an agent performing setup read exit 0 as success and carried on unauthenticated. The hint fires exactly when it matters -- fresh install, rotated secret, new machine, expired token. This skill emits no auth_instructions field, so these hints are the only setup guidance it gives. The replacements name the real command and, in doctor, the variables `auth login` actually reads: FALCON_CLIENT_ID and FALCON_CLIENT_SECRET (plus the optional CROWDSTRIKE_OAUTH_SCOPE), taken from the login command's own env fallbacks rather than composed. Reported by @geekbrownbear, who verified halopsa and ninjaone live against an empty config (PR #277) and filed appdirect/crowdstrike as issue #278; the fleet scan that found the other two surfaces and confirmed only these four connectors are affected was done during triage. GENERATOR-class defect: until the press is fixed, a reprint reintroduces all 7 strings and these asserts guard them. Bug-fix-only: no new flag, command, or output field.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: DONE UPSTREAM: mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#4315 closed as completed 2026-08-25 ('already fixed on current main': the oauth2 auth hint names `auth login` since PR #2875, merged 2026-06-08, first shipped press v4.25.0); this hand-fix stays active until a reprint absorbs it, and the helpers.go and MCP tool-error surfaces must be re-checked at that reprint because upstream's closure named only doctor's auth_hint and the usage error; do NOT cite #4315 as open. Encoded there: Derive the auth hint from the subcommand set the connector actually generates instead of the fixed "Run '<cli> auth setup' for credential setup steps." string in internal/generator/generator.go. 52 of 56 connectors do define `auth setup`, which is why the hard-coded string went unnoticed; the four OAuth client-credentials connectors that scaffold `auth login` instead (appdirect, crowdstrike, halopsa, ninjaone) each shipped it 7 times. The same string is emitted into three surfaces -- doctor.go's auth_hint, helpers.go's 400/401/403 remediation, and the MCP server's tool-error text -- so a generator fix must cover all three.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For crowdstrike the manifest gained: CROWDSTRIKE_BASE_URL, CROWDSTRIKE_TOKEN_URL. server.json gained: CROWDSTRIKE_BASE_URL, CROWDSTRIKE_TOKEN_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: CROWDSTRIKE_BASE_URL, CROWDSTRIKE_TOKEN_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: CROWDSTRIKE_NO_CONFIG_WRITE makes every credential write a no-op (token cache included) while leaving the `auth logout` erase working, and the MCP server honours it too (issue #270)
handfixes.why: Issue #270, raised by @Xenith-B off the back of #266. #266 stopped env-supplied client credentials reaching disk; the MINTED access token still landed in ~/.config/<tool>-cli/config.toml in cleartext and there was no supported way to turn that off. Their workaround was `--config NUL`, which is OS-specific, undocumented, makes doctor report a false 'not configured', and - the part that matters most - does not cover the MCP servers at all, because internal/mcp resolved its own hardcoded config path and ignored --config. Three deliberate boundaries make this switch honest rather than merely quiet. (1) ClearTokens keeps calling save() directly: it is the ERASE path, and routing it through the guard would make `auth logout` silently inert, which is a worse defect than the one being fixed. (2) `auth login` and `auth set-token` REFUSE and name the variable rather than reporting a save that did not happen - a false success is the same defect class as a doctor that says credentials are fine without checking. (3) newMCPClient now resolves through config.Load(""), the resolver the CLI uses, so the MCP server honours both CROWDSTRIKE_CONFIG and this switch; that is the half the issue says is uncovered today. The variable is declared on all three install channels because for a Claude Desktop install the manifest prompt is the ONLY channel that can set an environment variable. Class C, new documented surface. GENERATOR-class: a reprint drops the switch entirely and silently restores the plaintext token cache.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit <PREFIX>_NO_CONFIG_WRITE (or an equivalent) as part of the standard config surface, with the same three boundaries: the erase path exempt, explicit save commands failing loudly rather than no-oping, and the MCP server resolving its config through config.Load("") instead of a hardcoded home-relative path. The hardcoded path in internal/mcp/tools.go is a generator defect in its own right - it makes --config and <PREFIX>_CONFIG inert for every MCP install on every connector.

handfixes.summary: The MCP shell-out layer refuses `fleet tenants --expected`, which names a file on the machine that runs the MCP server, by listing it in blockedDestinationFlags
handfixes.why: `fleet tenants --expected` names a newline-delimited CID list the CLI reads off the local disk. The MCP server runs this CLI as the account that hosts it and forwarded the flag, so one tool call could point the read at any file that account can reach and get the parsed rows back. Reproduced on origin/main d3cbf7129 (connector tree unchanged at 518e1edff) with the real MCP binary and a recording stand-in for the companion CLI: tools/call with the flag set reached the CLI argv. The flag's usage text did not say it took a path, so isFilesystemPathFlag missed it and TestNoShellOutToolCanDirectAFilesystemPath stayed green; the usage text now says 'Path to', which makes that test fail until the floor names the flag, so a reprint that drops this entry fails the build. The operator still passes the flag on the command line. Found while vetting the gosec G304 finding its `#nosec G304` annotation hid from the security gate.

handfixes.summary: Every token request (auth login, the automatic client-credentials mint and the refresh grant) goes through cliutil.OAuthTokenHTTPClient, which follows same-origin redirects only, so the client secret never reaches a host a redirect from the token URL names
handfixes.why: Owner decision on PR #441 (finish the auth-wire class). `auth login` (through http.DefaultClient) and the automatic client-credentials mint and refresh grant (through c.HTTPClient, whose CheckRedirect follows a 307 to another host) replayed the token request body, the client secret included, to whatever host a redirect from the token URL named. Printed before press 4.33.5, which routes every token request through cliutil.OAuthTokenHTTPClient (a token client that follows same-origin hops only); this back-ports that file verbatim and uses it at the same call sites. TestAuthLoginRefusesATokenRedirectToAnotherOrigin and TestTokenMintRefusesARedirectToAnotherOrigin failed on the previous commit (the second host received the token request) and pass now. The host compare is also hardened (see the newer-print entries): an IP literal compares exactly, IPv6 zone included; a DNS name folds ASCII case only.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: auth.go.tmpl and client.go.tmpl in press 4.33.5 already route token requests through cliutil.OAuthTokenHTTPClient; oauthTokenSameOrigin should compare IP literals exactly (zone included) and fold ASCII case only for DNS names.

handfixes.summary: `fleet sync --member-cid` mints its child-tenant token through cliutil.OAuthTokenHTTPClient, so a redirect from the token URL to another host never receives the client secret
handfixes.why: Codex review round 3 on PR #441, confirmed by the owner as a secret leak: fleetClientForCID built a plain http.Client for the scoped member-CID mint, and Go replays the form (client_id, client_secret, member_cid) on a 307 to another host. With FALCON_CLIENT_ID/FALCON_CLIENT_SECRET set and the token endpoint answering 307 to a second port, `fleet sync --member-cid <cid>` sent the secret there. handfixes.summary: Every token request (automatic mint, refresh grant, auth login, the fleet member_cid mint) resolves its URL through client.ResolveCrowdStrikeTokenURL: a safe CROWDSTRIKE_TOKEN_URL, else /oauth2/token on the configured cloud's host (CROWDSTRIKE_BASE_URL), else US-1 when nothing is configured; an unsafe or untrusted route resolves to no URL and nothing is posted
handfixes.why: Each Falcon cloud (US-1, US-2, EU-1, US-GOV-1) serves its own token endpoint at <cloud>/oauth2/token. Press 4.34.2 hard-codes https://api.crowdstrike.com/oauth2/token at all three generated token sites, so an operator who set only CROWDSTRIKE_BASE_URL to EU-1 or GovCloud posted the client ID and secret to US-1 (0.1.10 did the same; only fleet sync derived the URL, without any safety check). tools/apply_edits.py re-points the three generated sites; fleet_sync.go calls the resolver directly.

handfixes.summary: One client_credentials token form (client.ClientCredentialsTokenForm: grant_type, client_id, client_secret, optional member_cid and scope) for the automatic mint, auth login and the fleet member_cid mint; no HTTP Basic header
handfixes.why: CrowdStrike's /oauth2/token takes client_id and client_secret as form fields (FalconPy's oauth2.token sends them in the body; 0.1.10 did too). Press 4.34.2 renders HTTP Basic client authentication, which the vendor does not document; an unverified auth scheme on the one request every command depends on is a silent-401 risk with every gate green (press-traps s5). Not live-verified either way: no vendor credentials.

handfixes.summary: fleet sync's child-CID clients present only the member_cid token minted for that CID: the child config is pinned (client.PinToken), so its client never mints, refreshes or swaps in the parent pair's token, and the member_cid mint client is origin-pinned to the token URL; the minted token is held by the credential kit as it arrives.
handfixes.why: fleet sync builds each child client from a copy of the parent config with the client pair cleared. The generated client falls back to FALCON_CLIENT_ID/FALCON_CLIENT_SECRET, and the token binding (minted-token-bound-to-its-client) would then mint, or reuse from process memory, the PARENT token for that config: the child CID's rows would hold the parent tenant's hosts, alerts and vulnerabilities, a wrong result an MSP acts on per tenant. tokenBinding returns 'no mint' first for a pinned config.

handfixes.summary: doctorShippedBaseURL is empty: https://api.crowdstrike.com is the real US-1 Falcon API, so doctor dials it and probes the credential instead of reporting 'base_url is still the shipped placeholder' on every healthy default install
handfixes.why: Press-traps s5: the fleet doctor-verdict template set doctorShippedBaseURL to the connector's default base URL, which for CrowdStrike is the real US-1 API. tools/apply_post_replay.py re-applies it after a fresh replay.

handfixes.summary: sync keys host-shaped records by device_id: the spec carries x-resource-id device_id on /devices/combined/devices/v1, /devices/combined/devices-hidden/v1, /devices/combined/host-group-members/v1 and /policy/combined/prevention-members/v1

Encoded in the spec (tools/spec_fix.py), so it survives every reprint.

handfixes.summary: fleet sync's member_cid mint and every child-CID client are built like every other client: the mint goes through the guarded plain transport auth login uses (CROWDSTRIKE_CA_CERT / TLS server name, dial guard, plaintext-credential refusal via client.GuardTokenRequest) and the token-client pin (API origin, plus only the token POST on another token host); each child client gets --dry-run, the TLS check and the client hooks (origin pin, response hold, no response cache)
handfixes.why: Tests-helper finding of the 4.34.2 reprint (adapting the ported credential suite), four defects in one class (a hand-built client skipping the shared construction): child clients were built with client.New alone, so the on-disk response cache stayed on and child responses echoing the member_cid token were written to cache/http (seen/fleet-child-client-unguarded-cache-seen-failing.log, fleet-child-client-guarded-blackbox); `fleet sync` against an http:// base URL off loopback posted client_secret in the clear (fleet-mint-plaintext-refused); the mint used the default transport so CROWDSTRIKE_CA_CERT was ignored (fleet-mint-honors-ca-cert); guardTokenClient pinned only the exact token path, so the shipped same-origin redirect test failed (member-cid-same-origin-redirect).

handfixes.summary: A *_url configuration key (token_url, base_url) is a URL setting: the credentials the URL carries are held (credkit.HoldURL, handfixes.json credkit-url-credentials-held), the URL itself is not, so a config.toml naming its Falcon cloud's token endpoint still saves and prints.

A posture snapshot (fleet trend) is recorded only for a CID whose hosts, alerts and vulnerabilities were all read completely in the same sync. (Codex r2 narrowed it: only a scope the read proves, see fleet-replace-only-a-proven-scope; the Flight Control fabric is upserted, and the authenticated CID is replaced only bound to its client.)

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand and replaces this connector's own credential layer. internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one Declarations literal; each main starts with credkit.Start and ends with credkit.Exit (the MCP main's body returns every exit code to it); the MCP server reads stdio through credkit.MCPIn, writes through credkit.MCPOut, runs every tool under credkit.MCPTools and serves HTTP through credkit.MCPHTTP; every API, token, fleet, feedback, deliver and probe request goes through credkit.Transport (cliutil.OutboundGuard; for the API client under the origin pin, so the guard judges what is really sent); every file write except the 0600 credential store and the config files goes through the kit (cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile is that declared exemption); a config file read again after startup is held by credkit.HoldBody before it is parsed; the MCP server's CLI children and the macOS ACL helper run through credkit.RunCommand; the MCP HTTP server's own --tls-key material is held before it serves (bound to no origin). CredentialFields leaves out client_id (the first field of the token form; its value is held from every source it comes from) and ResponseFields names every credential a Falcon response can carry.
handfixes.why: The hand-wired layer (cliutil/crowdstrike_output.go, crowdstrike_secrets.go, crowdstrike_decoded.go, crowdstrike_scattered.go, secret_funnel*.go, the store's withholding driver and the cli and mcp filters, ported from appdirect) duplicated what the kit now owns for every connector. One contract, one matcher and one set of sinks replace it, and a matcher fix reaches this connector by vendoring. Seen failing on the layer and passing on the kit: TestKitMCPHTTPWithoutATokenSaysWhy (a token-less --transport http launch exited 1 with nothing on stderr: os.Exit cut the filter pipe) and TestKitDoctorJSONIsAVerdict (the layer withheld the whole doctor --json document). Seen failing with the kit wiring removed: TestKitMCPIncomingHeldBeforeDispatch (MCPArguments), TestKitMalformedConfigHeldBeforeStartupOutput (Files and the parse holds), TestKitMCPHTTPTokenNeverPrinted (SecretEnv), TestKitJournalHoldsNoCredential.

handfixes.summary: The learn journal keeps no text the operator typed in place of a declared name: the CROWDSTRIKE_LEARN_SESSION override is stored as "o:" plus the same 64-bit SHA-256 hash the harness session ids get under "h:"; argv_shape records only flag names the invoked command declares under exactly the typed name and every other name as the "<undeclared>" placeholder (redacted), and nothing after "--"; failed_flag is never kept as typed ("--<undeclared>" when Cobra matched it to a declared flag, otherwise dropped); teach.log's missing --query lines record argument counts. Every journal line is appended through credkit.AppendFile, so one that repeats a held credential is withheld too. journal_credential_hardening_test.go drives each path with a credential, not held and held, and fails if it reaches any file under the test home.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.2 (learn/journal.go.tmpl) returns the override raw from JournalSessionKey, so a credential set there is written to journal-*.jsonl on every command, version included, and records every typed flag name, so a credential typed as a flag name (or after --) becomes an argv_shape key and the failed_flag; teach.log records the raw arguments of a teach with no --query. TestJournalCredentialHardening failed on the generated code (19 subtests). Known limits: a guessable override can be confirmed by hashing guesses; entries an older build wrote stay until the 14-day retention deletes their segment; recall and teach query text is kept as the press designs it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: learn/journal.go.tmpl should hash the LEARN_SESSION override as it hashes harness ids, and JournalArgvShape should take the invoked command's declared-flag lookup and record any other name as a placeholder, stopping at "--"; the failed flag should be the placeholder too, and teach.log should not echo raw arguments.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. retired.reason: tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0 keeps the environment markers through SaveTokens and generates MarkCredentialsExplicit, so a client ID or secret read from the environment is never written by a token save.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0 builds a per-command blocked set (blockedDestinationFlags, blockedInputFlags, root control-plane flags), removes those flags from each tool's schema, refuses any undeclared argument name (so "db=/path" is refused) and skips '=' names in cliArgsFromMCP.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Upstreamed as cli-printing-press #4647: every value-carrying branch of cliArgsFromMCP joins the value to its flag (--k=v, one element per list item), and the press generates TestCliArgsFromMCP_ValueCannotSmuggleBlockedFlag.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: The note paused HTTP mode until a reprint because the build served HTTP with no token. tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0's cobratree mirror derives one blocked set per command (destination, input, mcp:write-flags, mcp:read-flags and root control-plane flags), leaves those flags out of the tool schema and refuses them, and any undeclared argument, by name.
